beginner.summary: For platform engineers, system administrators and developers who are new to HashiCorp Consul and need to run it for service discovery in a single datacenter. Covers the dev agent, server and client agents, agent configuration, bootstrapping a three-server cluster, service registration and health checks, the DNS interface and HTTP API, blocking queries, the KV store, sessions and locks, watches, consul-template, gossip and Raft basics, gossip encryption, TLS for agent traffic, ACL bootstrap and policies, the web UI, snapshots, and a capstone that wires a three-tier application together through Consul.
prerequisites: Comfortable on a Linux shell: systemd units, editing files, curl, dig and reading JSON with jq
Understands basic networking: IP addresses, TCP and UDP ports, DNS records (A and SRV) and HTTP status codes
Has a laptop with Docker or three small Linux VMs and rights to install the consul binary
outcomes: Install Consul, run a dev agent and bootstrap a three-server cluster with a healthy Raft leader
Register services with health checks and discover them through Consul DNS and the HTTP API
Store and watch configuration in the KV store and render it into files with consul-template
Secure a cluster with gossip encryption, TLS and default-deny ACLs, and back it up with snapshots
